claims.claim: Parker-Hannifin's motion/control and filtration portfolio sits between industrial/aerospace equipment needs and reliability, fluid-management and contamination-control bottlenecks; the August Filtration Group close broadens that control surface rather than creating a new end need.

The causal thesis is resilient only if acquired filtration capabilities improve critical-application/aftermarket reach without integration complexity eroding operating gains; substitutes remain alternative component suppliers, customer insourcing and redesigned systems that reduce component intensity.

risks.risk: Portfolio breadth creates integration and execution dependencies; resilience improves only if acquired capabilities translate into durable customer/application leverage.

unknowns.unknown: Post-close filtration synergy realization and exact cross-selling contribution remain unobserved.

claims.claim: Current primary evidence strengthens execution credibility through record FY2026 sales, organic growth and margin performance, but does not yet prove the prospective FY31 margin target or Filtration Group synergies.
The most decision-useful falsifier is sustained failure to convert acquisition breadth and organic growth into expected margin/cash benefits; present uncertainty is not itself a blocker.

risks.risk: Acquisition integration, portfolio complexity and customer alternatives can reduce expected synergy and pricing benefits.
FY31 margin ambition is a forward benchmark, not present evidence of achievement.

unknowns.unknown: Financing and acquisition-accounting effects require Alpha underwriting and are not inferred here.
